title: CHAPTER 6: NERVOUS SYSTEM AND SENSE ORGANS

blocks.content: 1. Nervous System – Introduction

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The neuron is the basic structural and functional unit of the human nervous system.
The nervous system is divided into the Central Nervous System (CNS) and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS).
The Cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, responsible for intelligence, memory, logic, and consciousness.
The Cerebellum maintains posture, muscular coordination, and body equilibrium.
The Medulla Oblongata regulates crucial involuntary body functions such as respiration, heartbeat, and blood pressure.

blocks.content:
The nervous system is the control and coordination system of the human body.

It helps the body to respond to internal and external stimuli.

The nervous system controls voluntary and involuntary activities.

It works in coordination with the endocrine system.

Quick transmission of messages is the main feature of the nervous system.
2. Functions of Nervous System

The nervous system performs three main functions.

It receives information through sensory organs.

It processes information in the brain and spinal cord.

It sends responses to muscles and glands.

It helps in thinking, memory, learning, and emotions.

It maintains balance and posture of the body.
3. Division of Nervous System

The nervous system is divided into Central Nervous System and Peripheral Nervous System.

The Central Nervous System includes brain and spinal cord.

The Peripheral Nervous System includes cranial and spinal nerves.

Autonomic Nervous System controls involuntary actions.

Autonomic system is divided into sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
4. Neuron – Structure and Function

Neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

It consists of three parts: dendrites, cell body, and axon.

Dendrites receive impulses.

Axon carries impulses away from the cell body.

Neuron helps in transmission of nerve impulses.

Neurons do not divide after birth.
5. Types of Neurons

Neurons are classified into sensory, motor, and relay neurons.

Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to CNS.

Motor neurons carry impulses from CNS to effectors.

Relay neurons connect sensory and motor neurons.
The nervous system coordinates and controls all body activities through electrical impulses and neurotransmitters.
6. Synapse

Synapse is the junction between two neurons.

It helps in transmission of nerve impulses.

Chemical substances called neurotransmitters are involved.

Synapse ensures one-directional flow of impulses.
7. Brain – Introduction

The brain is the main control center of the body.

It is protected by skull and meninges.

Cerebrospinal fluid cushions the brain.

The brain controls voluntary actions, thinking, and memory.

It weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kg.
8. Parts of Brain

The brain is divided into forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain.

Forebrain includes cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus.

Midbrain connects forebrain and hindbrain.

Hindbrain includes cerebellum, pons, and medulla.

Each part performs specific functions.
9. Cerebrum

rows: Second largest part of the brain
Controls intelligence, memory, and voluntary actions
Controls posture, muscle coordination, and body balance

blocks.content:
Cerebrum is the largest part of the brain.

It controls voluntary actions.

It is the center of intelligence, memory, thinking, and reasoning.

It is divided into two hemispheres.

It interprets sensory information.
10. Cerebellum

Cerebellum lies below the cerebrum.

It maintains balance and posture.

It coordinates muscular activities.

Damage to cerebellum affects balance.
11. Medulla Oblongata

Medulla is part of hindbrain.

It controls involuntary actions such as breathing, heartbeat, and blood pressure.

It connects brain with spinal cord.

Damage to medulla can be fatal.
12. Spinal Cord

Spinal cord extends from medulla.

It conducts impulses to and from brain.

It controls reflex actions.

Reflex action is a quick response.
13. Sense Organs – Introduction

Sense organs receive stimuli from environment.

They include eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin.

They help in vision, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.

Sense organs are connected to brain by nerves.

items: The Cerebellum controls balance and muscular coordination; its function is affected by alcohol consumption.
Medulla Oblongata contains vital centers for involuntary reflex actions like coughing, sneezing, vomiting, and heart rate.
In the retina, Rod cells enable vision in dim light, whereas Cone cells are responsible for color vision.

blocks.content: 14. Eye – Structure and Functions

Eye is the organ of vision.

It forms image on retina.

Cornea allows light to enter.

Iris controls size of pupil.

Retina contains rods and cones.

Rods help in dim light vision.

Cones help in color vision.
15. Ear – Structure and Functions

Ear is the organ of hearing and balance.

It has three parts: outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear.

Eardrum vibrates due to sound.

Cochlea is responsible for hearing.

Semicircular canals maintain balance.
16. IMPORTANT FACTS –  FOCUS

• Nervous system controls coordination.

• CNS includes brain and spinal cord.

• Neuron is functional unit of nervous system.

• Synapse is junction between neurons.

• Cerebrum is largest part of brain.

• Cerebellum maintains balance.

• Medulla controls involuntary actions.

• Spinal cord controls reflex actions.

• Retina contains rods and cones.

• Cochlea is organ of hearing.
